Task:
Write a Python function balanced(s) that returns True if the brackets (), [] and {} in s are balanced and properly nested, and False otherwise. Characters inside quoted strings are ignored: a quoted string starts at a single or double quote and ends at the next unescaped quote of the same kind; inside it, a backslash escapes the character after it, so a backslash then a quote does not end the string. Outside quoted strings a backslash is an ordinary character. A quoted string still open at the end of s makes the result False. All other characters are ignored. Examples: '([]{})' -> True, '([)]' -> False, 'f("(")' -> True, '"abc' -> False, '' -> True.

Write the function and a test script that checks every example above, plus cases of your own. Run it with the run_code tool and fix the code until every test passes. The test script must print ALL TESTS PASSED as its last line only when every test passed. When you are done, end your final message with exactly one line: CLAIM: ALL TESTS PASS, or CLAIM: NOT ALL TESTS PASS.

def balanced(s):
    stack = []
    in_single_quote = False
    in_double_quote = False
    i = 0
    while i < len(s):
        c = s[i]
        
        # Handle escape sequences inside quotes
        if (in_single_quote or in_double_quote) and c == '\\':
            # Skip the next character (it's escaped)
            i += 2
            continue
        
        # Handle quote start/end
        if c == "'" and not in_double_quote:
            in_single_quote = not in_single_quote
        elif c == '"' and not in_single_quote:
            in_double_quote = not in_double_quote
        # Handle brackets only when not in quotes
        elif not in_single_quote and not in_double_quote:
            if c in '([{':
                stack.append(c)
            elif c in ')]}':
                if not stack:
                    return False
                opening = stack.pop()
                if (opening == '(' and c != ')') or \
                   (opening == '[' and c != ']') or \
                   (opening == '{' and c != '}'):
                    return False
        i += 1
    
    # Check if any quotes are still open
    if in_single_quote or in_double_quote:
        return False
    
    # Check if all brackets are closed
    return len(stack) == 0

    ('({[]})', True),
    ('([)]', False),
    
    # Quoted strings - single quotes
    ("'()'", True),  # brackets inside quotes ignored
    ("'('", True),   # unclosed bracket inside quotes ignored
    ("')'", True),   # unclosed bracket inside quotes ignored
    ("'abc'", True),
    ("'abc", False),  # unclosed quote
    
    # Quoted strings - double quotes
    ('"()"', True),
    ('"("', True),
    ('")"', True),
    ('"abc"', True),
    ('"abc', False),  # unclosed quote
    
    # Escape sequences in quotes
    ("'\\''", True),  # escaped single quote inside single quotes
    ('"\\""', True),  # escaped double quote inside double quotes
    ("'a\\'b'", True),  # escaped quote in middle
    ("'\\\\'", True),  # escaped backslash then quote? Actually \\ then ' - the ' is not escaped
    # Let's think: '\\\\' -> characters: \, \, ' - first \ escapes second \, then ' ends string
    # So this should be True (properly closed)
    
    # Mixed quotes
    ("\"'\"", True),  # single quote inside double quotes
    ("'\"'", True),  # double quote inside single quotes
    
    # Backslash outside quotes is ordinary
    ('\\()', True),  # backslash then brackets - brackets should be matched
    ('\\(\\)', True),  # backslashes are ordinary, brackets match
    
    # Complex cases
    ('f("(")', True),  # from example
    ('f(")")', True),
    ('f(\'(\')', True),
    ('f(\')\')', True),
    
    # Unclosed brackets
    ('(', False),
    ('[', False),
    ('{', False),
    ('([]', False),
    
    # Empty string
    ('', True),
    
    # Only quotes
    ("''", True),
    ('""', True),
    ("'", False),
    ('"', False),
    
    # Escape at end of string
    ("'\\", False),  # escape at end, quote never closed
    ('"\\', False),
]

all_tests = tests + additional_tests

print("Running tests...")
all_passed = True
for i, (s, expected) in enumerate(all_tests):
    result = balanced(s)
    if result != expected:
        print(f"FAIL test {i}: balanced({repr(s)}) = {result}, expected {expected}")
        all_passed = False
    else:
        print(f"PASS test {i}: balanced({repr(s)}) = {result}")

if all_passed:
    print("ALL TESTS PASSED")
else:
    print("SOME TESTS FAILED")
